rows.requirement: An absolute path outside the workspace is rejected by reads and write planning; an approved absolute-path write leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A `..` traversal out of the workspace is rejected by reads and write planning; an approved traversal write leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A path containing a NUL byte is rejected: reads report outside the workspace, write planning reports the NUL byte, nothing is invoked and canaries are unchanged.
A sibling directory sharing the workspace root's name prefix is outside the workspace (separator-prefix confusion).
A symlinked ancestor directory is never followed by reads, resolution or writes; an approved write through it leaves the outside canary unchanged.
A symlink as the final path component is never followed by reads, resolution or writes, and the link is retained.
A directory swapped after the scope guard decided (preallocated sibling plus rename) fails closed for read and list; replacement content is never returned.
A parent directory substituted at any write phase (before and after the temporary file, before the rename) never lets the write reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
A parent directory substituted before removal never lets a delete reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
A parent directory substituted before failed-write cleanup never lets cleanup reach the outside-root or guard-denied sibling canaries (#552).
The host exec child environment is exactly the documented allowlist (PATH, HOME, LANG, USER, TMPDIR); unrelated parent secrets never appear.
Agentflow children receive only the baseline allowlist, explicitly approved names and runner-owned values; a parent secret never reaches the real gate (#577).
An MCP stdio server child receives exactly the policy environment names and configured values, and no parent canary (#578).
A bwrap-confined payload sees exactly the approved environment set (PATH, HOME, TMPDIR and the PWD bwrap sets); a parent sentinel never appears.
rows.exempt: the native-profile mutation needs a Linux host with bwrap: PR #478 (e4d580b3) records bwrap confinement mutations but none for the payload environment set. Follow-up, tracked in the PR body: on a Linux host with bwrap, apply an M-ledger-style mutation that lets a parent variable through the bwrap payload environment, run GO_LLM_REQUIRE_BWRAP=1 go test -count=1 -run '^TestBwrapPayloadEnvironment$' ./agent/tools, record it in docs/security/containment-mutations.md and cite it here

rows.requirement: The Seatbelt backend replaces every TMPDIR entry with the private per-run directory and keeps a hostile inherited TMPDIR out of the profile. This is the TMPDIR helper and wrapper contract, not a complete native child-environment probe.
Approval previews render ESC, C1, carriage return, backspace, tab and bidi controls inert and visibly escaped, for file, exec and background prompts.
Streamed terminal rendering quotes control sequences in model tokens and tool-result previews (#433).

Approval previews render terminal controls inert on the real producer paths (write_file path and content, edit_file content and context, path headers, exec argv and cwd) and, for verification commands, at the approveVerify boundary (#387).
A changed argv after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed working directory after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed sanitized environment value after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
A changed resolved executable path after an exec grant requires fresh approval.
An executable swapped between Plan and Invoke (sibling plus rename, a new inode) fails closed and the runner is never called.
A different executable at the same resolved path after an exec grant requires fresh approval (#420 trust hardening).
A same-path script-content change after an exec grant requires fresh approval (#420 trust hardening, not the fingerprint).
MCP tool approvals are never grantable: every call prompts.
submit_plan lock approvals are never grantable: every call prompts.
A file grant (/auto-edits) never authorizes execution.
An exec grant never authorizes a file mutation.
A foreground exec grant never authorizes a background start (exec and exec-bg keys are partitioned).
Verifier grants and exec or file grants never cross-authorize, even under an identical key.
A one-time approval covers exactly one call; the identical repeat prompts again.
With a nil approver, mounted write and exec tools fail safe: nothing is written or executed.
A headless run mounts no write or exec tool without an explicit -allow-tool authorization.
Forged and marker-looking context delimiters in tool observations stay literal bytes inside a per-request nonce frame (exact-byte fixtures).
MCP tool descriptions reaching the model through Connect and the adapter are normalized and capped at 8 KiB: exact, hostile and multibyte cases.
MCP tool results reaching the model observation are capped at 32 KiB of flattened bytes with a preserved prefix: below, at, above, straddle and structured cases.
A changed MCP tool catalog is refused against its trust-on-first-use pin, and a stale-digest approval is rejected without rewriting the pin (#432).
Project guidance reaches the model only with matching live consent; a changed or unapproved document is omitted (#431).
Approved AGENTS.md guidance enters the system message only through the #431 trust gate, fenced as PROJECT_CONTEXT; it is excluded from the model corpus (R2).
Zero-width smuggling is tagged for workspace origin and blocked for foreign origin, raw and escaped.
Base64 (four alphabets, folded) and hex encoded instructions are tagged or blocked by origin; weak phrases stay tags.
Exact and typoglycemia-scrambled instruction phrases are tagged or blocked by origin; weak phrases stay tags.
All nine secret kinds are blocked from every origin, and secret-bearing tool arguments are blocked before dispatch.
Default argument invariants block protected and credential paths, ambiguous spellings and piped remote-script execution, in a fixed order; allowed and delegated cases pass.
Exec egress classification tags privileged, network, package-manager, interpreter and unknown commands with fixed risks; these are tags, never a denial.
Interceptors run in the fixed default order after blocks and errors; a tool-call block precedes dispatch and a tool-result block precedes the observation.
Each hook's RiskReport snapshot is owned by the run and unaffected by later findings.
The canary detector finds the run nonce in content, thinking and tool-call output in any case, and an activated session binding detects it (#438).
An allowed read followed by a granted export to a local surrogate sink, with only the always-on guards active.
An allowed read of a secret-bearing file followed by a granted export, with the full default interceptor chain and canary on.
A secret read into the model context and written back inline is blocked by the Secrets interceptor before the write lands.
A workspace edit to a previously granted script followed by its foreground execution requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit to a previously granted script followed by its background start requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit followed by a previously granted verifier command requires fresh approval (#420).
A workspace edit followed by an ungranted verifier command prompts, and a denial blocks it.
A poisoned but validly signed memory record is recalled only as fenced, unreviewed tool data, never in system or instruction position.
Memory promotion requires approval (#471).

rows.requirement: Labeled tool-loop traces cover the four attacker goals in blunt and helpful forms across the original #452 strata, with allowed behavior and attack-success criteria per stratum.
Per-model InjectionResistance and RestraintUnderAttack are reported alongside AnswerQuality with paired deltas and bootstrap confidence intervals.
Marker validation reuses the integrity-canary approach; fixtures carry no live secrets and reports do not expose planted values.
Model resistance is reported separately from runtime containment, which the scenario registry evaluates independently.
At least one end-to-end artifact per stratum is manually reviewed and recorded, with the corpus stratification documented.
The coverage inventory names an assertion, a scenario or an artifact for every requirement and distinguishes verified, pending and unsupported behavior; markers and refs are lint-bound.
